newsitem.title: USA: NYC, NYS near pact on new finance agency - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC, NYS near pact on new finance agency - paper.

text.p: New York City and New York State are near to reaching agreement on a new infrastructure authority that would let the city borrow up to $7.5 billion over the next four years, New York Times reported Friday.
The final agreement could be reached Friday or Monday, the paper said, but added officials close to the deal, who declined to be named, cautioned it still might encounter last-minute obstacles.

The agreement is expected to follow along the lines of a plan proposed by Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhatttan. A new agency was proposed by the city to sidestep a state-imposed limit on how much debt the city can issue, which it is expected to hit as soon as April, the paper said.

Over the next four years, the city would have to win an amendment to the state constitution that would change the debt formula, which now hinges on a five-year average of property values, to one that included revenues from other taxes, including personal income taxes, or get the legislature to extend the debt cap and life of the new agency.
